# Cursor launches Origin, its own GitHub alternative

Cursor launches Origin, GitHub alternative

▲ 52tomasreimers17 HN discussion

Cursor launches Origin, its own GitHub alternative

Cursor is rolling out Origin, a new code hosting service in early beta for all paid plans. It offers repos, pull requests, code browsing, and GitHub sync, with agent-native features coming soon. Origin repos live in a new Codebase tab, and GitHub repos can be synced alongside them, with real-time updates and two-way PR comments. Apps like Vercel, Depot, and Buildkite integrate for previews and CI. Cursor aims to bring code, PRs, and agents together in one place.

> Your code, PRs, and agents are now in the same place.

results.title: "If GitHub was stable, these alternatives would not be as interesting": Cursor launches Origin as GitHub goes dark
results.content:
PUJI NINGSIH for Unsplash+

Cursor has officially thrown its hat into the code-hosting ring with Origin, a Git-compatible platform built for a world where AI agents generate the commits.

The beta launch announced late on Monday comes two months after Tomas Reimers took to the stage at Cursor’s developer conference in San Francisco to tease its agent-focused GitHub alternative. That happened to be on the very same day that Elon Musk’s SpaceX confirmed it had tabled a $60 billion bid to acquire Cursor outright, and with that deal formally closing on August 14, Origin becomes the first product Cursor has shipped as a fully-owned SpaceX subsidiary. [...] At launch, that starts with the basics. Users can create and host Git repositories directly inside Cursor, with the new Codebase tab acting as the home for Origin repos.

Cursor Origin lets users create and host Git repositories directly inside Cursor.

Cursor Origin lets users create and host Git repositories directly inside Cursor.

Those repositories still behave like Git repos outside Cursor. Developers can clone them locally, add an Origin remote, and push code from the command line — essentially putting Cursor in the role normally occupied by a service such as GitHub.

Pushing a local repo to Origin

Pushing a local repo to Origin [...] Tomas Reimers, the Origin engineer who co-founded Graphite, a code-review startup Cursor acquired in early 2026, fielded questions directly from developers on Hacker News after the launch.

> “We’re intentionally releasing this as a GitHub alternative where we meet them toe-to-toe on functionality.”

Asked what set Origin apart from GitHub beyond uptime, Reimers concedes that it’s very “very little,” in all honesty. “We’re intentionally releasing this as a GitHub alternative where we meet them toe-to-toe on functionality,” he writes.

Agents do not just generate code, they create branches and open PRs like humans do. Or review changes and kick off CI/CD scripts, but much faster than humans would.
That's why many developers are looking into what the control system for agentic code should be.
Former GitHub CEO Thomas Dohmke started Entire to rethink software development for an agent-heavy world.
Cursor recently unveiled Origin as an agent-first alternative to GitHub.
And now OpenAI seems to be investing deeper into Git too.

Shane Spencer, graphic

Origin is Cursor's agent-native Git platform, announced today, built on the Graphite team they acquired late last year. Available this fall, waitlist open now. The live demo showed 22.6 commits per second in a single repo plus hundreds of thousands of clones and pushes per hour, numbers aimed at the moment when many agents are editing one codebase at once.
The competitive subtext: GitHub, VS Code, and Copilot are all Microsoft. Building on GitHub means depending on a direct competitor at the hosting layer.
If you run agent workflows, where's your review-and-merge bottleneck right now?
